summary: Frontend-only regression + motion-enhancement validation for Lumen Event Management landing (15 sections + 2 dashboards + mobile). All 15 review items PASS. ZERO page errors. Two non-blocking framer-motion console warnings (useScroll container non-static position) observed but do not affect functionality. Verified: ScrollProgressBar fills (scaleX matrix(0.04,...) after small scroll), Hero aria-label='Experience Events Like Never Before' present and matches review note, BrandsMarquee dark 2-row tape contains both 'Premium Events' and 'AURORA' words, LiveCounters animate to final values 48,214 / 2,400,000 / 84 / 4.96, CategoriesExplorer renders, FeaturedEventHero with Aurora Tech Summit text present, WhyLumenHorizontal section height=4536px (≈4.2x viewport, expected ~4.2vh height ratio for 420vh), 6 why-panel-01..06 testids present, panel 01 left position moved from +157.8px to -1664.8px on half-section scroll confirming horizontal translateX works, StickyCtaBar appears after hero scroll showing 'Aurora Tech Summit · 72% sold' with Register + Close, sticky-cta-close dismisses it, /dashboard and /admin routes load without regression, mobile 375/390px hamburger toggle opens navbar-mobile-menu correctly, FAQ toggle clicks, testimonial prev/next clicks work.

issues: Two framer-motion warnings: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative, fixed, or absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' These originate from useScroll target refs in Hero and/or WhyLumenHorizontal. Functionality works correctly; the parent should be set to position:relative explicitly to silence the warning.

Hero heading wrapper computed transform reported as 'none' at scroll=0 and scroll=540px because useTransform sets scale=1.0 -> identity, and the parent <motion.div style={{ y, opacity }}> wraps it. The headingScale animation only kicks in noticeably near end of hero (~scrollY ≈ innerHeight). Functionally the scale animation is wired correctly; it just isn't perceptible at 50% viewport scroll. Not a bug — just an animation curve note. Consider widening the scale range (e.g. [1, 0.85]) or starting earlier if more visible parallax is desired.

design_issues.screen: Hero heading SplitReveal (carried over from iter 2)
issues: data-testid='hero-heading' textContent still concatenates as 'ExperienceEventsLike Never Before' (no literal space between SplitReveal words). Now mitigated for tests via aria-label='Experience Events Like Never Before' which matches exactly. ✓ The review-note workaround works.

action_items: (Low priority) Add `position: relative` (or `style={{ position: 'relative' }}`) to the useScroll target containers in Hero.jsx and WhyLumenHorizontal.jsx to eliminate the two framer-motion console warnings.
(Optional) Widen Hero headingScale range from [1, 0.92] to [1, 0.85] (or start the scale earlier) so the parallax is more perceptible during normal hero exit scroll.
critical_code_review_comments: ScrollProgressBar uses useSpring on scrollYProgress with sensible stiffness/damping — confirmed scaleX transform updates on scroll (matrix(0.04,...) at small scroll).

MagneticCursor correctly guards against touch + mobile (matchMedia hover:none OR width<1024) and renders nothing on mobile. No initial visible cursor on first render — only after first mousemove (opacity:0 -> 1), as designed.

WhyLumenHorizontal uses sticky-top track inside a 420vh section; horizontal translateX confirmed working via measured panel left positions. Bottom progress bar uses scaleX with transformOrigin 0% 50% — correct pattern.

StickyCtaBar threshold (scrollY > innerHeight*0.9 and not nearBottom) works; close button sets dismissed=true on local state (per-page-load, not localStorage). For a true 'per-session' dismissal, consider persisting to sessionStorage.
BrandsMarquee uses 3x-duplicated children and CSS keyframes -33.333% translate for seamless loop — standard, no jank.
LiveCounters RollingNumber animation cap is 1.6s with quartic ease-out — clean values after settle.

Two framer-motion warnings about non-static container in useScroll: minor, but should be fixed by ensuring target refs have an explicit non-static position (relative). Hero <section> uses className 'relative' so should be fine — warning may come from WhyLumenHorizontal's <section> which does have 'relative' too; warning may still trigger due to nested measurement timing. Worth a quick code inspection.
App.js mounts ScrollProgressBar and MagneticCursor globally above Suspense — correct (no flash on route change).
